title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This sheet is not Grothendieck's handwriting. It is a typed, mimeographed Bourbaki draft ('rédaction n° 382', p. 82), photographed upside down. It is most likely the verso of a sheet whose other side Grothendieck used for his handwritten notes. The surrounding pages are his manuscript calculations on Dieudonné modules of Barsotti–Tate groups with an action of a ramified p-adic ring A (h = ef, dim G_0 = 1 iff F^f is a uniformiser, Lubin–Tate-type classification); this page is unrelated to them. The draft covers foundations of differential geometry: jets and jets of sections. 7.1.12: for C^r manifolds X, Y, r' ≤ r and finite k ≤ r', weakening the structure to C^{r'} commutes with forming jet spaces. That is, J^k(X',Y') is J^k(X,Y) with its C^{r-k} structure weakened to C^{r'-k}. Section 7.2 'Jets de sections': for a submersion π: Y → X, P^k_x(X,π) is the set of k-jets f at x of maps X → Y with j^k(π)∘f equal to the jet of the identity. Equivalently, these are k-jets of germs of local sections. For finite k, P^k_x and their union P^k(X,π) are closed submanifolds of J^k_x(X,Y) and J^k(X,Y). The source, target and source-target fibrations of J^k(X,Y) induce fibrations of P^k(X,π). When π is a vector bundle E, P^k(X,E) is a vector bundle over X. It is also a module bundle over the algebra bundle P^k(X) of principal parts. For a trivial bundle F_X, P^k(X,F_X) ≅ P^k(X) ⊗ F_X ≅ J^k(X,F). 7.2.3: truncation J^k → J^{k'} induces P^k(X,π) → P^{k'}(X,π), a morphism of fibrations over X. For a vector bundle, the kernel of P^k_x(X,E) → P^{k'}_x(X,E) is identified with a space of jets; the sentence is cut off, but presumably jets vanishing to order k', i.e. ⊕_{k'<i≤k} S^i T*_x ⊗ E_x. This is the standard jet-bundle / principal-parts formalism, written in Bourbaki's 'Variétés différentielles et analytiques' style.
errors: The bases of the induced fibrations are typed as 'π(X)×Y, π(X) et Y'. Since π: Y → X, the expression π(X) is ill-defined. The source-target map of P^k(X,π) lands in the graph of π (≅ Y), and the source map lands in X. This is probably a typo in the draft (perhaps for X×Y, X and Y, or a misprinted symbol). Not Grothendieck's error.
The final sentence of 7.2.3 is cut off at the page break, so the identification of the kernel is incomplete on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed Bourbaki draft on jet bundles, used as scrap paper, likely the verso of Grothendieck's sheet. Its content is standard foundational material with no connection to the neighbouring handwritten Dieudonné-module computations.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down, i.e. rotated 180°. It is a typed Bourbaki rédaction (n° 382, p. 82), not Grothendieck's manuscript.
In 7.2.2, the symbol in 'bases respectives π(X)×Y, π(X)' is as typed but likely a draft typo; the image shows the same symbol.
